 Oct 30, 2026 
 NLEX goes for sweep, Phoenix tries to extend series
 PHOENIX Super LPG aims to turn its “down but not out” mindset into game when it fights for survival against NLEX Saturday in their PBA Governors Cup quarterfinals duel at the Ninoy Aquino Stadium.
 By virtue of hard-earned wins in the best-of-five matchup’s first two games the Road Warriors now have three chances to close the deal and advance to their first semifinals stint since the 2021-22 edition of the same tourney.
 Wrapping up the series via the shortest route would also help allay most of NLEX’s immediate concerns.
 “The series isn’t done. That’s why it’s a race-to-three,” said coach Jimmy Alapag, himself close to becoming the first head coach in his first conference, since TNT’s Jojo Lastimosa in the 2022-23 Governors Cup, to make at least the semifinals.
 “Same mindset going to Game 3, watch the film tonight, see how we can be better.”
 Schonny Winston also has a guarded approach, mindful as he is of what happened to NLEX in the last Commissioner’s Cup, when it topped the eliminations only to blow a twice-to-beat advantage to eighth-ranked TNT.
 “We’ve been in a similar situation before and we just got to continue to just stay humble and our head down and keep working hard,” said Winston.
 Indeed, coach Charles Tiu remains adamant they could at least extend the series despite the dire straits he and his FiberXers are in.
 “Obviously, not an ideal situation. But until the series is over, we’re gonna keep on fighting. We’d still compete. We’ll be ready Saturday, when we’ll play our best game,” said Tiu moments after a 117-124 loss in Game 2 last Wednesday.
 Adding to Tiu’s optimism is the fact that his side put up a much better performance in Game 2 that prevented the Road Warriors from reprising a wire-to-wire 97-92 loss in the series opener.
 Sponsored content: 
 “We had a bit of a better game, but kulang pa. But at least may improvement na,
 noted Tiu.
 Definitely not about to ease his foot off the pedal and exhorting his NLEX teammates to do the same is Robert Bolick.
 “As much as possible, dito na kami eh, nag-zero na. Bakit pa pagbibigyan pa?” the star guard posed. “Habang medyo down pa sila, go for the kill na lang. Hopefully, ma-execute namin.” (NC)
